rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Maximum Rent Increase
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quote: Your landlord can only raise your rent by a certain amount each year. The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.summary: Landlords may increase rent by a maximum of 3% or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is less, each year.
rules.key_value: 3% or 80% of CPI, whichever is less

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quote: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
rules.summary: Landlords must have a valid reason to evict tenants, such as non-payment of rent, lease violations, or owner move-in.

rules.title: Santa Ana Relocation Assistance for Certain Evictions
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quote: If your landlord evicts you for certain reasons, they might have to help pay for your moving costs.
rules.summary: Landlords may be required to provide relocation assistance to tenants evicted for certain reasons.
